notes:
Lead: Maya Chen (AE). SE: Liam Patel. CSM: Olivia Grant.

Background: Cobalt Regulatory Labs builds automation for regulatory filings across NA/EU, heavy PII/FIN datasets. Engaged Redwood for Private VPC deployment to host inference for document classification, summarization and downstream risk scoring. Procurement is fast-moving but security and legal scope are strict.

What they asked for (high level):
- Private VPC with customer-managed control plane (no public control-plane endpoints).
- KMS BYOK + HSM attestation: keys must be customer-controlled; key rotation policy required.
- Full audit logging for all model requests & admin actions; retention configurable up to 7 years and exportable to their SIEM (Splunk).
- Data residency: EU tenant required for EU customer datasets; must support multi-region tenancy (us-east-1 + eu-west-1).
- SIG/CAIQ: customer sent vendor risk intake (SIG) + expects CAIQ mapping. Redwood to provide completed CAIQ matrix and shared-responsibility table.
- Network: support for VPC peering or PrivateLink; restricted egress for model weights and no outbound to public internet for inference traffic.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 Type II + ISO27001 certs requested (redacted copies acceptable).

Recent timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-02-02: Intro call (AE+SE) — high level requirements captured; asked for architecture options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink).
- 2026-02-14: Deep dive with Cobalt security (Fireflies ff_2026-02-14_CRL-call-1298) — collected SIG baseline, agreed CAIQ deliverable.
- 2026-02-28: SE architecture walkthrough — discussed KMS BYOK flow, HSM attestation needs, and audit log export mechanics.
- 2026-03-05: Pricing + draft SOW delivered (drive:/contracts/cobalt/draft-sow-2026-03-05.docx).
- 2026-03-10: Legal/Procurement requested indemnity clause examples and exact SLA for key availability.

Technical notes / commitments discussed:
- Proposed architecture: private control plane in customer VPC, worker nodes in a dedicated subnet, private endpoints via PrivateLink, S3 endpoints for model artifacts with VPC endpoint.
- KMS model: BYOK with support for AWS KMS and external HSM (PKCS#11) integration. Key rotation and a backup/rotation policy doc promised by SE.
- Audit logging: request/response and admin actions logged; logs sent to customer-managed S3 + CloudWatch -> Splunk; retention policy configurable.
- Shared responsibility: Redwood to own runtime security, kernel selection patches, and model hosting hygiene; customer responsible for network security, IAM for KMS keys, and data classification before ingestion. SE to produce an explicit shared responsibility matrix.

Customer quotes / color: "We cannot have model outputs escape our EU tenant." — Head of Compliance.
"Need firm answers on BYOK SLA and if keys can be revoked immediately without residual copies." — Platform Security.

Open asks (actionable):
- Completed CAIQ + SIG baseline due from Redwood by 2026-03-17.
- Provide HSM attestation example + BYOK SLA language for legal.
- Confirm PrivateLink architecture diagram and flow for model artifact access.
- Prepare shared-responsibility table for legal & security to sign off.

Next steps (practical):
- SE to finalize CAIQ mapping and upload to drive (target 2026-03-15).
- AE to schedule vendor risk intake call w/ Cobalt security (wk of 2026-03-17).
- Legal to review proposed indemnity redline and BYOK SLA language (target 2026-03-22).

Other notes: procurement timeline sensitive — they need SOW + PO in April to hit internal FY milestones. Customer is price-sensitive but prioritizes security controls over unit cost.

Staged POC suggestion: start with non-PII dataset (EU residency) for classification POC in eu-west-1, validate KMS flow and log export, then broaden to production dataset once legal signoff complete.
